dossier.public_summary: The signal is not a stable planet. Alternate transits and whole sectors show very different depths, with some sectors showing no dip at all, and the odd and even dips differ strongly. A small star or blended binary eclipse varying between sectors fits the data better than a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even dips differ by 6.25 sigma with a factor 3.6 depth difference (528 ppm), opposite to a single-period planet. Sector check shows no odd-even signal overall indicating the difference is driven by sector depths, but the raw alternate-deep alternate-shallow pattern remains a strong binary indicator.

Depth is not steady. Sector 42 is consistent with zero depth (28 +/- 80 ppm) while sectors 31 and 71 are deep ~700-785 ppm, indicating the signal is present in some sectors and absent in others. This is not a stable planetary transit.

Depth change persists within the same light-curve source (SPOC 2-min sectors 31: 785 ppm vs 42: 28 ppm), ruling out a calibration between sources. Requires a real astrophysical change or blend, not a planet with steady depth.

Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent. One epoch is essentially no transit, the others are deep, inconsistent with 4 observed at 14.2 d period on the target. Indicates only a few blended or binary events make the average signal.
